settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url) is invoked before parsing (Xml.java:70), but it only rejects file: URLs when import.file.enabled is false; it does not block HTTP URLs or entity resolution targets
Some JVMs / deployments set system-wide JAXP hardening properties (javax.xml.accessExternalDTD etc.), which are not visible in this repository
candidates.description: In src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java, `xmlXpathToMapResult` constructs a `DocumentBuilderFactory` and sets only `setNamespaceAware(true)` and `setIgnoringElementContentWhitespace(true)` (lines 65-68), then parses caller-supplied content via `documentBuilder.parse(Util.openInputStream(url, headers, null))` (line 74). No `setFeature` calls disable `http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl`, external general/parameter entities, or `XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING`. If the underlying parser does not default to secure processing, a crafted XML document fetched from an attacker-controlled URL could reference external entities or external DTDs. The same class also uses a shared static `XMLInputFactory FACTORY` with only `IS_COALESCING` set (line 39, 124). Root cause: XML parser factories are used without security-hardening features.
missing_evidence: No explicit EntityResolver/ErrorHandler is configured in Xml.java to neutralize external entity resolution
Cannot confirm from source whether any classpath-level JAXP default hardening property is present
Did not verify the runtime Xerces/JAXP version bundled by Neo4j 3.4.9
preconditions: A user able to invoke apoc.load.xml (or the deprecated xmlSimple / apoc.xml.import procedures) on the DBMS
The URL argument points to content controlled by the attacker (or a redirect to such content)
The runtime XML parser implementation defaults to resolving external entities/DTDs (Java default behavior for DocumentBuilderFactory is unhardened unless a JAXP property sets it)
candidates.title: Potential XXE in apoc.load.xml DocumentBuilderFactory without external entity / DTD hardening

counter_evidence: getStreamCompressedFile still uses getStreamConnection, so it ultimately respects the same protocol dispatch (http/s3/hdfs) rather than arbitrary local file reads
FileUtils.checkReadAllowed is called by the higher-level loaders (e.g. JsonUtil.loadJson:53) before openInputStream
candidates.description: `Util.openInputStream` checks `if (urlAddress.contains("!")) return getStreamCompressedFile(...)` (lines 286-288) before deciding the protocol. `getStreamCompressedFile` splits on `!` and, for the remaining part, calls `getStreamConnection` -> `readHttpInputStream` / S3 / HDFS (lines 296-322). This means any caller-supplied URL containing a `!` is routed into ZIP entry extraction logic (`getFileStreamIntoCompressedFile`, lines 338-350), independent of the read-allowed/file-origin checks that other loaders apply via `FileUtils.changeFileUrlIfImportDirectoryConstrained`. Root cause: a syntactic character in the user-supplied URL changes the fetch/extraction code path without an equivalent guard.
missing_evidence: Did not trace every caller to confirm which ones skip checkReadAllowed
No test inspected to confirm expected behavior with '!' in URLs
preconditions: A user can invoke a loader/procedure that passes a URL into Util.openInputStream (e.g. apoc.load.json/xml/csv via JsonUtil.loadJson or Xml paths)
They control the URL string including a '!' character and the remote content
candidates.title: Literal '!' in input URL triggers compressed-file handling regardless of scheme and bypasses read-origin intent

counter_evidence: The procedure requires the caller to already have write access to the graph via procedure invocation
Neo4j property-key name restrictions still apply, limiting what can be written
candidates.description: `Xml.importToGraph` (annotation `@Procedure(mode = Mode.WRITE, value = "apoc.xml.import")`, line 397) reads XML from a caller-supplied URL via `getXMLStreamReaderFromUrl` (line 399 -> 121-126) and creates nodes, properties, and relationships from parsed element names, attribute names, and text (lines 429-455). Attribute names become property keys and element local names become node properties (`_name`, line 432). There is no restriction that the source be a trusted store, and `root.setProperty("url", url)` writes the raw URL (line 409). Root cause: a write-capable procedure consumes semi-trusted remote/derived XML and materializes it into the graph.
missing_evidence: Did not verify DBMS-side procedure allow-listing/security configuration for this version
No confirmation whether callers are restricted to admins
preconditions: A user with permission to call a WRITE-mode procedure
Ability to supply a URL whose content they influence
candidates.title: apoc.xml.import write procedure ingests untrusted XML into graph without origin/type restrictions

counter_evidence: The confinement code exists and is effective when the config flag is enabled
Application-level file permission checks (`file.canRead()`) are still performed in readFile/readFileStream (FileUtils.java:75,81) and in the constrained branch (line 102)
candidates.description: `FileUtils.changeFileUrlIfImportDirectoryConstrained` only applies the import-directory confinement when `ApocConfiguration.isEnabled("import.file.use_neo4j_config")` is true (line 86); otherwise it returns the URL unchanged (line 109). Combined with `checkReadAllowed` (lines 137-139), which only blocks file reads when `import.file.enabled` is false, file access is not confined to the import directory by default. `isFile` returns true for almost any non-http/hdfs string, including plain paths. Root cause: security-relevant confinement depends on configuration flags that default to permissive behavior in the read path.
missing_evidence: Did not inspect ApocConfiguration defaults to determine the effective default values of import.file.enabled and import.file.use_neo4j_config
No runtime config file present to confirm deployed settings
preconditions: apoc.import.file.enabled=true (or equivalently the import.file.enabled property effective true)
A user can pass an arbitrary URL/path to a loader
candidates.title: Import directory constraint is opt-in; file reads are allowed by default when import.file.enabled
